expectations.evidence: The rewrite adds claims such as "tanking productivity and killing momentum" and "compounds across a team", and it changes the retro quote to "The cache mattered, but the benchmark told us what to fix" (original: "The cache was a game changer, but the benchmark is what told us where to look"); it also drops the "p95" qualifier on the 19-minute figure ("Now it finishes in 19 minutes").

It introduces stock phrasing like "a developer's worst enemy", the staged reveal "Here's what changed.", "Priya said it best", and a generic closing section "What changed" with "spend less time waiting and more time shipping".
Mostly short, concrete sentences with varied length, e.g. "The problem was obvious once we looked: we weren't compiling slowly. We were downloading the same dependencies over and over."
It stays in an engineering team blog register with plain, concrete statements like "We benchmarked all 11 services first" and no hype or jokes beyond the cliche opener.
